title: Why Sanitary Tees Fail in Horizontal Drainage Lines
description: Using a sanitary tee on a horizontal-to-horizontal drain connection is a common installation mistake that leads to frequent blockages. Sanitary tees are designed primarily for transitioning from horizontal to vertical flow. When placed flat on horizontal runs, the sweep direction does not adequately direct solids forward, causing waste to build up or splash backward into the branch line. Plumbing codes require a combination wye and eighth bend or a long-sweep wye for horizontal directional changes. Proper fitting selection maintains directional flow velocity and prevents recurring clogs. Always verify fitting orientation against code requirements before gluing.

Why Sanitary Tees Fail in Horizontal Drainage Lines

When placed flat on horizontal runs, the sweep direction does not adequately direct solids forward, causing waste to build up or splash backward into the branch line. Plumbing codes require a combination wye and eighth bend or a long-sweep wye for horizontal directional changes. Proper fitting selection maintains directional flow velocity and prevents recurring clogs. Always verify fitting orientation against code requirements before gluing.
